Which Price Bracket Is Right for You

If you're buying your first riding jacket, the Rs.6,000 to Rs.10,000 range is usually the sensible starting point. It covers CE Level 1 armour, a proper abrasion resistant shell, and decent ventilation, without paying for touring features you might not need yet. Going lower usually means compromising on armour quality or the shell material itself.

Once you're past Rs.10,000, you start seeing CE Level 2 armour as standard, better weatherproofing, and materials built for long days in the saddle rather than short commutes. If you ride mostly on weekend highway runs or plan longer tours, this is where most serious touring jackets sit.

Not sure whether you want mesh, textile, or leather before you pick a price bracket? Our guide to choosing a riding jacket covers material and fit in more detail than a price filter alone can.

FAQs

Q1: What is a reasonable budget for a first riding jacket?

A1: Jackets in the Rs.6,000 to Rs.10,000 range typically cover CE Level 2 armour, decent ventilation, and a proper abrasion resistant shell, enough for regular commuting and weekend rides. Going below that usually means compromising on armour quality or material.

Q2: What's the difference between the price brackets?

A2: Jackets under Rs.6,000 to Rs.8,000 are typically basic commuter options with essential armour. The Rs.8,000 to Rs.20,000 range is where most serious touring jackets sit, with CE Level 2 armour, better weatherproofing, and premium materials becoming standard. Above that, you're usually paying for premium brands or specialised features like adventure touring builds.

Q3: Can I filter jackets by size before deciding on a price range?

A3: Yes, every price bucket page lets you filter further by size, brand, and colour, so you don't need to browse the entire range to find what fits. It's worth checking size availability first, since some models sell out faster in specific sizes.

name: Short Cuff Biker Gloves
originalDescription:
Short cuff biker gloves stop at the wrist instead of covering it. That makes them the lightest and most breathable gloves you can wear, which is why most riders reach for them through the Indian summer and for everyday city commuting.

The trade off is wrist coverage. Below highway speeds, in stop and go traffic, that trade off is a fair one. Above it, a gauntlet glove is the safer call.

What you should still expect from a good short glove is hard knuckle protection, a palm reinforcement or slider, a secure wrist strap that actually holds under load, and touchscreen compatible fingertips if you navigate from your phone.

We stock short cuff gloves from Rynox, Raida, Axor, TVS Racing, Cramster, Scala, Furygan and RS Taichi. All genuine products with warranty, secured online shopping, and fast shipping across India.

How to choose a short cuff glove

  • For daily city commuting: prioritise mesh panels and airflow over armour bulk. You will wear them every day, so comfort decides whether they stay on your hands.
  • For weekend spirited rides: look for a hard TPU or carbon knuckle and a palm slider. These are the parts that do the work in a low speed slide.
  • For summer specifically: perforated leather or full mesh backs shed heat far better than solid synthetic panels.
  • On a budget: browse biker gloves under Rs. 3000, where most of our city riding options sit.

Riding outside city limits or touring? Compare these against full gauntlet riding gloves, which seal over your jacket sleeve. Want wrist coverage without going all the way to a full cuff? Look at semi gauntlet gloves instead.

For a full walkthrough of glove types, materials and protection levels, read our guide on choosing the right riding gloves.
